mentions.heading: Our business in China subjects us to unique operational, competitive, regulatory, and economic risks.
mentions.risk_name: China JV competition and restructuring losses
mentions.detail: China JV impairment $2.1B and equity losses $2.0B in 2024, $0.6B charges 2025; SGM expects more restructuring in 2026
mentions.quote: As a result of certain restructuring actions previously announced in December 2024, we recorded an other-than-temporary impairment of our equity interests of $2.1 billion and additional equity losses of $2.0 billion in the year ended December 31, 2024, and we recorded charges of $0.6 billion in the year ended December 31, 2025.

mentions.heading: Chinese government regulation and critical materials access
mentions.risk_name: Chinese regulation restricting critical materials access
mentions.detail: Chinese government may restrict non-Chinese access to critical materials; U.S.-China trade tensions; China integrated in global supply chain
mentions.quote: The Chinese government may adopt new regulations that may impact entities operating in China or the ability of non-Chinese entities to obtain critical materials from China, potentially with little advance notice.

mentions.heading: We benefit from many ongoing joint ventures and other strategic business relationships over which we may have limited control.
mentions.risk_name: EV raw material offtake obligation exposure
mentions.detail: Offtake agreements obligate purchases of EV raw materials; lower EV volumes or battery tech changes could hurt cash flows; supplier investments may lose value
mentions.quote: If we are unable to utilize or otherwise monetize the raw materials we are obligated to purchase under these offtake agreements, whether as a result of lower than expected EV production volumes, lower than expected rates of consumer adoption, changes in battery technology that reduce the need for certain raw materials, or other reasons, it could materially adversely affect our cash flows and increase our inventory.
